title: Produce the authoritative ledger of positively selected deterministic capabilities
description:
Produce one authoritative ledger for deterministic capabilities Eshyra has positively
selected to offer. The ledger is authoritative about Eshyra's commitments, not about the
rules source. The legacy magic-item executionReadiness/engine:F backlog may be reconciled
as a bounded candidate backlog but need not all become selected capabilities.
design:
2026-10-09 DESIGN (Claude Captain, survey at main 6f57be85). Profile: semantic-system (capability boundary truthfulness) within rules-clause-complete.
CURRENT STATE: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts carries only three rule-bound contracts (resolve-check-v1, resolve-concentration-v1, resolve-spell-upcast-v1) with RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_BINDINGS to rule records (model-facing via ruleAwareness / discovery packet), plus RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_DISPOSITIONS ('not-positively-selected' rows). MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY lives in deterministicCapabilityContract.ts. createDefaultToolRegistry (packages/core/src/orchestrator/tools.ts ~L178) registers DEFAULT_TOOLS (~70 tool modules under packages/core/src/orchestrator/tool*.ts). Non-tool deterministic engine paths exist too (character creation finalize/enforcement, level-up engine and its choice application, class resources, campaign binding resolution for rests/level-up, checkpoint/replay).
KNOWN TRUTHFULNESS DEFECT: resolve-check-v1 says 'Does not decide which modifiers apply' and residual 'The DM selects applicable modifiers', but since PR #637 (eshyra-r8en) resolve_check DERIVES the ability modifier and proficiency/expertise/half-proficiency/save-proficiency term from the actor's character sheet when skill/ability is given, and refuses caller-declared duplicates. The contract must be restated from the real tool contract, with a new revision ('resolve-check-v2'); every binding and reference to v1 moves to v2.
DECISIONS:
 D1 New internal module packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts exporting DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_INVENTORY: readonly entries, each EXACTLY ONCE: { revision, operationId, surface: {kind:'tool', name} | {kind:'engine', module, entryPoint}, category: 'state-integrity' (dice/RNG, arithmetic, atomic canonical mutation, resource accounting, identity/ownership, persistence/replay/rollback, visibility/authorization) | 'bounded-procedure' (a positively selected rules procedure), operation, requiredInputs, exclusions, residualDmInterpretation, runtimeOwner[], evidence[], ledgerContract?: revision }. For the three rule-bound contracts and the magic-item preflight the entry QUOTES the existing contract (spread/reference the object; never restate the same facts in different words). Read-only/query tools (lookup_rules, world_query, list_nearby_items, memory drilldown, ...) are included with category 'state-integrity' only if they enforce visibility/authorization; otherwise list them under a separate exported NON_CAPABILITY_TOOLS with a one-line reason each (e.g. 'read-only retrieval; makes no deterministic rules commitment'), so the closure test can account for every registered tool.
 D2 Every statement is derived from the tool's real input schema, description, and implementation (state functions it calls, refusals, what it does NOT decide). Exclusions and residual interpretation must name what the DM still decides. No statement may claim rules completeness. Prefer short, exact statements.
 D3 Closure evidence (the only closure claim, over Eshyra's own bounded registry): a test that every tool name in createDefaultToolRegistry() appears exactly once across inventory tool surfaces + NON_CAPABILITY_TOOLS, every inventory tool surface is registered, every RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS revision is referenced exactly once by an inventory entry, MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY is referenced once, revisions are unique, and every runtimeOwner/evidence path exists on disk. Engine (non-tool) entries are curated with evidence pointers; no closure claim over engine code.
 D4 Backlog separation: export a function (e.g. summarizeMagicItemCapabilityBacklog(records)) that computes, from the pack by query, the legacy magic-item executionReadiness/engine:F backlog (records, clauses, engine-pending, hook-carrying) as a separate report object whose doc and fields state it is an UNSELECTED candidate backlog: never counted as implemented and never as absent. Test it against the real pack by structural assertions (non-negative, internally consistent), not hand-copied counts.
 D5 Presentation boundary: do NOT add new RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_BINDINGS or change RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_DISPOSITIONS (that would change what the DM model is told and needs its own presentation decision). Only the resolve-check v1->v2 truthfulness correction changes model-facing text. In the report, list each disposition row (e.g. rule:long-rest, rule:death-saving-throws) whose operation now has an inventory entry, as input to a later presentation decision.
 D6 Registry: finding row engine-capability-ownership (sol:CAP-007, owner eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12, disclosed-dependency) -> 'accepted' with statusReasoning naming this inventory, its closure test, and the separate backlog report.
EXCLUSIONS: no new capabilities, no behavior change to any tool, no corpus-wide completeness claim, no per-tool behavioral tests beyond existing evidence pointers.
acceptance_criteria:
- One inventory enumerates every deterministic capability in force - the rule-bound contracts in packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts, MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY, and any other in-force deterministic operation - each exactly once with the W13 contract fields (operation, required inputs, exclusions, revision/identity, residual DM interpretation).
- The bounded legacy magic-item engine:F backlog is reported separately from in-force capabilities, and unknown/unbound/unselected entries never count as implemented or absent.
- Completion proves the in-force capability set is truthfully stated; it does not prove deterministic completeness of the SRD.
notes:
Bead-writing contract (plan §VI) — this bead must state: exact scope membership
(explicit records/clauses or a deterministic query that enumerates them), root
cause, required invariant, source evidence, pack evidence, engine boundary,
regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias
list, and completion proof. "Fix the examples above" is not acceptable scope;
close the whole semantic class and reconcile exact membership.
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.

ROOT CAUSE of recurring omissions: engine entries were curated from memory, not from an independent population. Cycle-2 method: (a) mechanical candidate population = every module under packages/core/src/{state,character,campaign,checkpoint,memory,rules,orchestrator,adventure} with a production (non-test) caller, each dispositioned as covered-by-entry(X) or not-a-deterministic-commitment(reason), committed as a file-level disposition with a test that every such module file is accounted for (bounded population of files; no symbol census); (b) every claim in every entry must cite the code location it relies on (development log in bd notes); un-citable claims are removed. Implementation model escalated to Opus 5.5 for this cycle (repeated failure to close the class).
Fresh full review .9 at 598a730c (the review required after two repair cycles): CHANGES REQUESTED (2), accepted, same class, converging (6 -> 3 -> 2): S1 turn-transaction-v1 claims any tool error rolls back the turn, but recoverable ToolResult failures do not abort (toolRegistry.ts 226-243, turnLoop.ts 311-377, orchestrator.ts 1058-1102); S2 start_effect/refresh_effect duration statements generalize guards (instantaneous Find Familiar/Find Steed bonds are admitted, activeEffects.ts 3589-3668). Both are overreaching guarantee language. Decision: the full review has been performed; implementation proceeds on its findings with a targeted CLASS method: repair S1/S2 and their families (turn/audit/error; effect lifecycle start/refresh/end/suppress/remove), then audit every statement in every entry that uses a universal quantifier or guarantee verb (any, all, every, always, never, only, refuses/rejects, rolls back, atomic, idempotent, releases, persists, guarantees) against every branch of the cited code and narrow it to exactly what is guaranteed. Fresh Opus implementer (prior agent context near exhaustion). Fresh full Sol review after.
